newsitem.title: USA: Miami restaurant settles over ruined wine cellar.
newsitem.headline: Miami restaurant settles over ruined wine cellar.

text.p: A leading Miami restaurant on Monday reached agreement with an insurance company for $1.75 million in compensation for the destruction of its famed wine cellar during Hurricane Andrew in 1992, its lawyer said.
The case of the sour grapes has been in dispute since 1994 and was due to reach court in May.
"The Forge had the finest classic wine collection of any restaurant in the United States and was acknowledged as such. A hurricane destroyed it," lawyer Robert Shupack told Reuters.
Forge restaurant said when Hurricane Andrew hit, it knocked out the air-conditioning system that helped cool the cellar.
"The wine cooked because of the heat build-up in the cellar," Shupack said.

Bottles of wine were rendered undrinkable. Half the patrons of the upscale Miami Beach restaurant were sending back bottles of vintage wine, Forge wine steward Gino Santangelo said in the court records.

The primary insurance carrier paid out $1 million in compensation but Forge owners, Alvin Malnik and his son Shareef, claimed a further $2.9 million dollars for the loss of the wine and other structural damage from the second carrier, Transamerica Insurance Co.
Transamerica contested the figure and settlement was finally reached for $1.75 million, Shupack said.
The Forge is famed for its fine food and elegant decor. Regular patrons include pop star Madonna and actor Sylvester Stallone.
The Malniks could not be reached for comment.
